land.text: the West Saxon core on the south coast of England, which lies inside Cliopatria's single Anglo-Saxon England shape of 441-533 (41 of the 42 cells of Wessex's first shape)

predecessors.note: The Wessex infobox says 'Preceded by: Sub-Roman Britain, Gewisse, Kingdom of Kent'. Cliopatria hands the land over in 534; the page's founding year is c. 519 (see notes).

land.text: the whole of Wessex's last Cliopatria shape: Wessex, Kent, Sussex, Essex, East Anglia and Mercia, to which Æthelstan added York in 927

successors.note: The Wessex infobox ends the kingdom with 'the unification of the Angles, Saxons and Danes' on 12 July 927 and names the Kingdom of England as successor. Cliopatria keeps the Wessex row to 935 and starts its Kingdom of England row in 936 (see notes).

capitals.name: Winchester
capitals.note: Seat shown for the whole life, unverified: the Wessex infobox leaves 'Capital(s)' blank and the Æthelstan page says 'Anglo-Saxon kings did not have a fixed capital city'; the only Winchester fact on the pages opened is that Alfred died there on 26 October 899 (Alfred the Great infobox).

rulers.name: Cerdic
rulers.note: Infobox 'c. 519 to c. 534'; the page says he 'became first king in 519' (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

rulers.name: Cynric
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 534-560 (the Wessex page: he 'reigned for twenty-six years').

rulers.name: Ceawlin
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 560-591 (its chart and the Wessex page's Chronicle dates: 560-592; the Wessex page also says he 'succeeded Cynric in about 581').

rulers.name: Ceol
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 591-597 (the Wessex page gives no years).

rulers.name: Ceolwulf
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 597-611 (the Wessex page: 'in about 594').

rulers.name: Cynegils
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 611-643, ended here at 642 to meet Cenwealh's accession on the Wessex page (lead 'r. 642-645'); the Wessex page has Cynegils 'in about 617'. Cwichelm, a co-ruler c. 626-636, is not listed separately.

rulers.name: Cenwealh
rulers.note: Page lead 'r. 642-645, 648-672'; driven out 645, restored 648 (infobox: client state of Mercia 645 to 648).

rulers.name: Penda of Mercia
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 645-648 (Penda, King of Mercia); the Wessex infobox: 'client state of Mercia 645 to 648'.
rulers.title: King of Mercia, overlord of Wessex

rulers.name: Cenwealh
rulers.note: Second reign; the text puts his death in 673.

rulers.name: Seaxburh
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 672-674 (the Wessex page: she 'held the throne for a year' after 673).
rulers.title: queen regnant

rulers.name: Æscwine
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 674-676 (the Wessex page: his 'reign only lasted two years'). Cenfus (674) is marked 'Disputed' on the list and left out.

rulers.name: Centwine
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 676-685 (the Wessex page: accession 'in 676'; the Peonnum page has his victory over the Britons by 681-685).

rulers.name: Cædwalla
rulers.note: 'king of Wessex from approximately 685 until he abdicated in 688'; 'In either 685 or 686'; Bede gives two years. Fix (eu-11-d): from set to 685 (List of monarchs of Wessex: Cædwalla 685-688; this page: 'from approximately 685'); his conquests are dated 686 in the ledger.

rulers.name: Ine
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex and the Wessex infobox: 688-726; the Ine page and the Wessex lead give 689. Fix (eu-11-d): from set to 688 so the strip is contiguous with Cædwalla.

rulers.name: Æthelheard
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 726-740.

rulers.name: Cuthred
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 740-756.

rulers.name: Sigeberht
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 756-757 (deposed).

rulers.name: Cynewulf
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 757-786.

rulers.name: Beorhtric
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 786-802.

rulers.name: Egbert
rulers.note: 'King of Wessex from 802 until his death in 839'.

rulers.name: Æthelwulf
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 839-858.

rulers.name: Æthelbald
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 858-860.

rulers.name: Æthelberht
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 860-865.

rulers.name: Æthelred I
rulers.note: List of monarchs of Wessex 865-871 (the Alfred page: Alfred acceded in April 871 after Æthelred's death).

rulers.name: Alfred the Great
rulers.note: Acceded April 871 after the death of Æthelred; died 26 October 899 at Winchester.

rulers.name: Edward the Elder
rulers.note: 'Alfred died on 26 October 899 and Edward succeeded to the throne'; died 17 July 924 at Farndon.

rulers.name: Æthelstan
rulers.note: Last king of Wessex on the Wessex page (924-927); crowned 4 September 925 at Kingston upon Thames; King of the English from 927. Mercia accepted him in 924; Wessex 'may have' chosen his half-brother Ælfweard first.

correction.text: unchanged: Cliopatria's first Wessex shape (9,586 km2, southern Hampshire and the Solent coast), used for 519-533

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 519-533: Cliopatria's Wessex starts in 534, the year the page's infobox ends Cerdic's reign ('c. 519 to c. 534'). The page gives 'Established: c. 519' and says Cerdic 'became first king in 519'; its landing story (495, southern Hampshire) is 'not regarded by historians as reliable' and it dates nothing about land for 519-533, so Cliopatria's first shape stands in for those years. The page gives no area (infobox blank), so no area comparison is possible.

534-576, 9,586 km2. The page: after Cerdicesford (519) 'Expansion paused for about thirty years', which fits a small shape. The Chronicle's 530 conquest of the Isle of Wight is not drawn: Bede and the Cædwalla page put the conquest in the 680s and Cliopatria keeps the island in Wihtgar until 691. The page gives no area.

577-586, 17,279 km2: +30 cells (Wiltshire, Somerset, Bath) from the Brythons. Deorham: the Chronicle 'dates the battle to 577'; 'they killed 3 kings ... took 3 cities: Gloucester and Cirencester and Bath'. The shape holds Bath and Bristol, but Cliopatria gives the Gloucester-Cirencester land to its Hwicce shape from 577, which neither the Deorham page nor the Wessex page mentions; a gap-filler should decide whether Hwicce is a West Saxon vassal 577-586. The page doubts its own source ('importance given to these towns more likely reflects ninth and tenth-century polities'). Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2): Cliopatria's 577 shape holds 7 cells of Somerset (about 1,770 km2) that are exactly the cells of the county outside Cliopatria's Dumnonia shape. The Wessex page says Cenwealh (r. 642-672) 'was able to expand West Saxon territory in Somerset at the expense of the Britons', and the Peonnum page dates that to 658, so the cells are removed here and added back by the 658 gain. The Deorham page names only Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath.

correction.text: Wessex's shape without its seven cells of eastern and central Somerset east of the River Parrett, which were British until Cenwalh's victory at Peonnum in 658 (Battle of Peonnum: 'annexing eastern and central Somerset'); the Dumnonia dossier draws the same cells as Dumnonian until 657

keyframe_review.note: 587-627, 15,966 km2: Cliopatria returns 7 cells (Bristol to Gloucester) to the Hwicce. Neither the Wessex page nor the Deorham page mentions the Hwicce or any loss in the 580s, so the shape stands unverified (page silent). Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2): the same seven Somerset cells are removed until 657 (see kingdom-of-wessex_577).

correction.text: Wessex's shape without its seven cells of eastern and central Somerset east of the River Parrett, which were British until Cenwalh's victory at Peonnum in 658 (Battle of Peonnum: 'annexing eastern and central Somerset'); the Dumnonia dossier draws the same cells as Dumnonian until 657

keyframe_review.note: 628-665, 15,879 km2: three cells of the upper Thames go to Mercia. The pages opened do not date any Mercian-West Saxon fighting in 628; the infobox gives 'client state of Mercia 645 to 648' and independence 648-927, with no territorial change, so the shape stands unverified: page budget. The Mercian Supremacy page lacks Penda's wars with Wessex. A flicker of 2 cells at Maidenhead in 666 is ignored. Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2): correct for 628-657 only: the seven Somerset cells are removed until Peonnum (658). The 658-665 span is the new keyframe kingdom-of-wessex_658.

correction.text: Wessex's shape without its seven cells of eastern and central Somerset east of the River Parrett, which were British until Cenwalh's victory at Peonnum in 658 (Battle of Peonnum: 'annexing eastern and central Somerset'); the Dumnonia dossier draws the same cells as Dumnonian until 657
unchanged 628 shape for 658-665: Wessex with eastern and central Somerset as far as the River Parrett

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 658-665 (the tail of Cliopatria's 628-665 shape): the shape of 628 is correct from the year Cenwalh 'advanced west through the Polden Hills to the River Parrett, annexing eastern and central Somerset' (Battle of Peonnum: 'in 658 his army met the Britons for a climactic battle at Peonnum'; the infobox says about 660; the site is uncertain). The border 'remained at the Parrett until 681-685'. The gain is the ledger's 658 event; Dumnonia's 658 loss is its mirror.

correction.text: unchanged for 666-684: Wessex to the River Parrett, without western Somerset, Sussex, Kent or Wight

keyframe_review.note: 666-691 as drawn, 15,989 km2; correct only for 666-684. Cædwalla became king 'in either 685 or 686' and 'conquered the Isle of Wight', Sussex and Kent in his two-year reign, so the shape changes before Cliopatria's 692. See kingdom-of-wessex_685 and _686.

correction.text: Wessex plus western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel, taken under Centwine (by 681-685)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 685: Cliopatria's Wessex shape stops at the Parrett and never draws western Somerset until it takes Devon in 710 (where Dumnonia's 705 shape still holds it). The Peonnum page: the border 'remained at the Parrett until 681-685', when Centwine's victory let the West Saxons occupy 'western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel'; the Wessex page: Centwine 'fought and won battles against the Britons, but the details have not survived'. The 6 cells are the ledger's 685 gain (Dumnonia's 685 loss is its mirror) and stay in the shapes of 686-709.

correction.text: Wessex plus the Isle of Wight conquered under Cædwalla (686, with the Wessex page's c. 685-688); Sussex and Kent are ledger events (vassal, occupation), not part of the direct shape; plus the 6 cells of western Somerset held since 685

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 686-691: Wessex plus the Isle of Wight. The Wessex page: Cædwalla 'conquered Sussex, Kent and the Isle of Wight' in c. 685-688 and 'Kent regained independence almost immediately'. The Ine page: 'the South Saxons, who had been conquered by Cædwalla in 686' were kept 'in subjugation', so Sussex is a vassal in the ledger, not direct land; Kent is held only 686-688 (occupation events). Surrey: Cædwalla 'gained control of Surrey' (688 charter at Farnham), but Cliopatria's shape has held Surrey since 534 and no page dates an earlier Surrey; no cell change. Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2): the western Somerset cells gained in 685 are carried through 686-709.

correction.text: Wessex and the Isle of Wight without Kent (independent again) or Sussex (vassal 686-718), plus the 6 cells of western Somerset held since 685

keyframe_review.note: 692-704, 26,372 km2 as drawn: Cliopatria adds Kent (15 cells) and Sussex (23) and has no Kent row for 692-704. The Wessex page: 'Kent regained independence almost immediately, and Sussex followed some years later'; the Ine page: 'Ine made peace with Kent in 694 when its king Wihtred gave Ine a substantial sum' and kept Sussex 'in subjugation for a period'. Kent is therefore not Wessex land from 688 and Sussex is a vassal, drawn from the ledger. Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2): western Somerset (6 cells) is added to the corrected shape.

correction.text: Wessex without Sussex, which is a vassal until 718, plus the 6 cells of western Somerset held since 685

keyframe_review.note: 705-709, 21,580 km2 as drawn: Cliopatria restores Kent (its Kent row returns in 705) but keeps Sussex (23 cells) inside Wessex. The Ine page: 'Sussex was still under West Saxon domination in 710, when Nothhelm is recorded as having campaigned with Ine', i.e. a subject kingdom with its own men; vassal tint from the ledger, not direct land. Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2): western Somerset (6 cells) is added to the corrected shape.

correction.text: Wessex with Devon (from 710) but without Sussex, which is a vassal until 718

keyframe_review.note: 710-717, 31,168 km2 as drawn: +36 cells of Devon from Dumnonia. 'In 710, Ine and Nothhelm fought against Geraint of Dumnonia'; 'It has traditionally been thought that Ine's advance brought him control of what is now Devon'; the Wessex page says Wessex 'gradually overwhelmed Dumnonia' and held 'de facto control of much of Devon', Britons keeping some independence there to the 10th century. Sussex (23 cells) is still inside the drawn shape and is a vassal. Fix note (eu-11-d): of the 36 Dumnonian cells added in 710, 6 are western Somerset already held since 685, so the new Dumnonian land is 30 cells of Devon (31 cells as drawn, with one stray cell of Cliopatria's).

718-740, 26,217 km2: Sussex leaves. The Ine page has Sussex dominated in 710 and invaded in 722 and 725 ('Ine invaded Sussex'; 'Three years later Ine invaded again, this time killing Ealdberht'), so it was independent between; 718 is Cliopatria's year, bracketed 710-722. Surrey: the page says it 'had clearly passed out of West Saxon control' by Ine's time, but Cliopatria keeps Surrey inside Wessex and no page dates its loss; unresolved. 'The Battle of Hehil' (722, British victory, site unidentified) shows no border change.

correction.text: unchanged 740 shape: Wessex with Devon, without Sussex or Kent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 741-754: Cliopatria has no Wessex shape and its Mercia row grows to 74,610 km2 (about 48,306 km2 of Mercia plus Wessex's 26,217 km2), i.e. it swallows Wessex. The Wessex page says that in the 8th century 'Wessex largely stayed independent and may at times have acknowledged Mercian overlordship'; the Ine page puts Æthelheard in 'the sphere of influence of Æthelbald, the king of Mercia'; the Mercian Supremacy page: 'Æthelbald of Mercia restored Mercia's hegemony for over forty years'. Wessex is drawn with its 740 shape and a Mercian overlordship is for the Mercia dossier (vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart kingdom-of-wessex, not recorded here because the schema puts the vassal event in the suzerain's ledger).

755-762, 26,217 km2, the 718 shape again. The Wessex page: Mercia 'conquered the northern parts of early Wessex (Gloucestershire, Oxfordshire), so the Thames and Avon became the northern boundary', which the shape matches.

correction.text: Wessex south of the Thames and the Avon, as the 755 shape

keyframe_review.note: 763-782, 28,139 km2 as drawn: +9 cells north of the Thames (Oxford to Aylesbury) from Mercia, gone again in 783. The Wessex page says the Thames and Avon were the northern boundary after Mercia took Gloucestershire and Oxfordshire in the 8th century, so those cells are Mercian; use the 755 shape.

783-787, 26,458 km2: the 755 shape (100 cells). Matches the Thames-and-Avon boundary on the Wessex page. The Mercian Supremacy page credits 'Offa's defeat of the Welsh and the West Saxons' with establishing the supremacy but dates no battle (page silent on 779).

correction.text: unchanged 787 shape: Wessex south of the Thames and Avon

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 788-805: Cliopatria has no Wessex shape and its Mercia row grows to 84,530 km2 (788) and 96,899 km2 (800), swallowing Wessex. The Wessex page: Egbert acceded in 802 and Wessex was an independent kingdom throughout the century ('largely stayed independent and may at times have acknowledged Mercian overlordship'); the Mercian Supremacy page names Offa (757-796) and 'the end of the era ... around 825' and does not say Wessex was annexed. Wessex is drawn with its 787 shape; an overlordship for the Mercia dossier.

806-824, 25,932 km2: three cells of the Thames above London go to Mercia (event). Unverified: page budget; the Wessex page's 813 and 825 campaigns against the West Welsh do not move this shape (Dumnonia is already inside, Cornwall is a vassal from 825).

correction.text: Wessex with Kent, Sussex, Surrey and Essex but without independent East Anglia

keyframe_review.note: 825-829, 52,085 km2 as drawn: includes East Anglia (53 cells) and Essex (16), Kent and Sussex. The Egbert page: after Ellandun 'the men of Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex then all submitted' (the page disputes the speed: a Kentish charter of March 826 still names Beornwulf, and Essex's Sigered may have been expelled in 829); East Anglia, however, 'broke away' from Mercia, asked Egbert for protection in 825 (826 'more likely') and, the page suggests, its king Æthelstan killed Beornwulf (826) and Ludeca (827). East Anglia is therefore not Wessex land. Drawn for 825-828 only; 829 is the Mercia keyframe.

correction.text: Wessex plus Mercia for the single year 829

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 829: 'Ecgberht drove Wiglaf ... into exile, temporarily ruling Mercia'; the Chronicle: 'King Egbert conquered the kingdom of Mercia, and all that was south of the Humber'. Cliopatria dates this shape to 830-839; the page puts the conquest in 829 and Wiglaf's return in 830. East Anglia is excluded as above.

correction.text: Wessex, Kent, Sussex and Surrey, with Essex, without Mercia or East Anglia: the 840 shape plus the 16 Essex cells, which leave in 840

keyframe_review.note: 830-839, 96,899 km2 as drawn (the largest Cliopatria Wessex): includes Mercia (197 cells) and East Anglia (54). The Egbert page: in 830 'Wiglaf obtained the kingdom of Mercia again' ('likely a Mercian rebellion against West Saxon rule') and 'the expansion across south-eastern England proved permanent'. Mercia and East Anglia are independent again; drawn as the 840 shape (Wessex with Kent, Sussex, Surrey). The Egbert page also has Northumbria submitting at Dore in 829 (vassal event 829-830) and 'a successful expedition against the Welsh' in 830. Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /keyframe_review/19): the 840 shape alone dropped the 16 Essex cells that 825-829 draw as West Saxon with no event. The Egbert page hedges Essex after 830 ('Wessex retained control of the south-eastern kingdoms, with the possible exception of Essex'; 'Wiglaf may also have brought Essex back into the Mercian orbit during the years after he recovered the throne'), so Essex is kept in 830-839 and leaves in 840 (ledger loss, confidence 1, Cliopatria's year: its Wessex shape loses the 16 cells and its Mercia 840 shape holds them).

840-874, 35,983 km2: Wessex (including Devon), Kent and Sussex. The Egbert page: 'Wessex kept Kent, Sussex, and Surrey, which were administered as a subkingdom under Æthelwulf. Essex is uncertain'; Cliopatria gives Essex (16 cells) to its Mercia row from 840, which the page neither supports nor refutes. Cornwall is a vassal (ledger), not in the shape. The 851 Danish defeat at Aclea moved no border. The ledger records the loss of Essex to Mercia in 840 (confidence 1).

correction.text: unchanged 840 shape: Wessex with Kent and Sussex

keyframe_review.note: 875, 35,121 km2 as drawn: Cliopatria cuts 6 cells of the south coast between Weymouth and Southampton Water (Viking settlements) a year before the Danes took Wareham. The Alfred page dates the seizure of Wareham to 876; nothing opened shows Danish land in Wessex in 875.

correction.text: the full 840 shape; Wareham and Exeter are a contested zone, not Danish land

keyframe_review.note: 876-877, 34,371 km2 as drawn: Cliopatria cuts 9 cells (Wareham and Exeter) for the Danes. The Alfred page: 'The Danes under Guthrum, Oscetel and Anwend seized Wareham in 876, broke their oath, and moved to Exeter'. The held ground is drawn as a contest (ledger 876-878), so the direct shape is the full Wessex.

878-879, 35,434 km2: 'January 878 Chippenham', Alfred's refuge on the Somerset Levels (Wessex page), then Edington (878), after which the Danes 'withdrew to East Anglia' (Wessex page). The remaining Danish cells in the drawn shape are the pocket the contest ends in 878.

880-883, 35,939 km2: Wessex, Kent and Sussex again. The Alfred page puts the Alfred-Guthrum treaty 'perhaps in 879 or 880' with a boundary 'up the Thames to the Lea, ... to near Luton, ... to Bedford, ... the Ouse to Watling Street', which leaves London and the east to the Danes. Fix (eu-11-d): from 880 English Mercia is a vassal of Alfred (ledger): the Alfred page has Alfred 'succeed to Ceolwulf's kingdom consisting of western Mercia' when Ceolwulf II was deposed, 'perhaps in 879 or 880'; Cliopatria still draws it as its own Mercia row until 883.

correction.text: Wessex, Kent and Sussex; English Mercia is a vassal until 918

keyframe_review.note: 884-885, 57,728 km2 as drawn: Cliopatria adds all of English Mercia (92 cells). The Alfred page says only that Alfred gave London to his son-in-law Æthelred, ealdorman of Mercia (886), and never calls Mercia part of Wessex; the Edward page has Æthelred's death in 911 and Edward then taking 'the Mercian lands around London and Oxford', and the Wessex page has Edward taking 'direct control of Mercia in 918', which implies indirect control before. Drawn as a vassal (ledger 880-918, from the Alfred page's 'perhaps in 879 or 880'), not direct land; Cliopatria folds the 92 cells into its Wessex shape only in 884.

correction.text: Wessex, Kent, Sussex and London; English Mercia is a vassal

keyframe_review.note: 886-891, 58,691 km2 as drawn: the 884 shape plus London (5 cells). 'In 886, Alfred reoccupied the city of London' (and 'King of the Anglo-Saxons' from 886). Mercia is a vassal; London stays in the shape although the Alfred page says it was handed to Æthelred of Mercia (a 5-cell question for the gap-filler).

correction.text: as 886: Wessex, Kent, Sussex and London; the Kent coast is a contested zone

keyframe_review.note: 892-895, 56,754 km2 as drawn: six cells of the Kent coast go to the Vikings. The Alfred page: the invasion of 'the autumn of 892 or 893', Farnham, Buttington and 'the 894-895 blockade'; the Vikings left in 896 or 897. Drawn as a contest (ledger 892-896); the direct shape is whole.

correction.text: Wessex, Kent, Sussex and London; English Mercia is a vassal

keyframe_review.note: 896-897, 58,691 km2 as drawn: the Vikings leave ('departure in 896 (or 897)'). Mercia is a vassal.

correction.text: as 896

keyframe_review.note: 898, 58,778 km2 as drawn: one-cell flicker at Gloucester; Mercia a vassal.

correction.text: Wessex, Kent, Sussex and London; English Mercia is a vassal

keyframe_review.note: 899-910, 58,691 km2 as drawn: Alfred dies 26 October 899 and Edward succeeds; Æthelwold's revolt (Wimborne, Christchurch) ends with his death in 902 and the Danes' victory at the Holme (13 December 902) moves no border. Mercia a vassal under Æthelred (to 911).

union.text: Oxford and its Mercian lands, taken by Edward in 911

correction.text: Wessex, Kent, Sussex, London and Oxford; English Mercia beyond is a vassal under Æthelflaed

keyframe_review.note: 911-921, 58,426 km2 as drawn; correct for 911-917. 'Æthelred's death 911: Edward took control of the Mercian lands around London and Oxford'; Æthelflaed ruled the rest as Lady of the Mercians (911-918); Tettenhall (910) and the burhs (Hertford 911, Witham 912, Buckingham 914) hold the line. From 915 Edward takes the Danelaw (ledger); Cliopatria dates its conquest to 922.

correction.text: unchanged 922 shape (Wessex, Kent, Sussex, Mercia, East Anglia, the East Midlands to the Humber), holding from 918, not 922

keyframe_review.note: 922-925, 96,296 km2 as drawn; correct from 918. The Wessex page: Edward 'overwhelmed the Danes of Mercia and East Anglia between 913 and 918' and 'took direct control of Mercia in 918, after Æthelflaed died'; the Edward page has the Danish armies of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia submitting in 917 and Leicester in early 918. The shape is Cliopatria's, brought forward four years. Its Danelaw remnant to the north (from the Humber area to the Tees) stays Danish until 927.

correction.text: unchanged 926 shape

keyframe_review.note: 926, 96,384 km2: for 926 only. The Wessex infobox ends the kingdom on 12 July 927 and the Æthelstan page has the same hand: 'King of the Anglo-Saxons (924-927)' then 'King of the English (from 927)'; Cliopatria's row runs to 935 and England starts in 936. 928-935 belong to kingdom-of-england (see notes).

correction.text: Wessex's last shape plus the York lands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 927: Wessex's last shape plus York. 'Sihtric died in 927 ... Æthelstan then invaded and took York'; Eamont on 12 July 927 (Constantine II, Hywel Dda, Ealdred of Bamburgh and Owain of Strathclyde 'accepted his overlordship'). The Danelaw remnant of Cliopatria's 922-935 shapes (Humber to Tees, 70 cells) is the land taken; Northumbria proper (Bamburgh) is not annexed.

region.text: the West Saxon core on the south coast of England, southern Hampshire to Wiltshire: the Chronicle has Cerdic and Cynric landing in southern Hampshire in 495, 'not regarded by historians as reliable'

ledger.note: 519: Cerdic becomes the first king of the West Saxons. 'Cerdic became first king in 519' (Chronicle), infobox 'Established: c. 519' and reign 'c. 519 to c. 534'; after Cerdicesford (519) 'Expansion paused for about thirty years'. The page names no territory for 519; Cliopatria's Wessex shape begins in 534.

region.text: Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath: 'took 3 cities: Gloucester and Cirencester and Bath'

ledger.note: 577: the West Saxons win at Deorham. 'Here Cuthwine and Ceawlin fought against the Britons, and they killed 3 kings, Coinmail, Condidan and Farinmail' and 'took 3 cities: Gloucester and Cirencester and Bath' (Chronicle, 577); the only evidence is the Chronicle, which the page says is not a contemporary record. Cliopatria keeps only the Bath-Bristol part inside Wessex. Confidence 2 (reviewer eu-11-d): the page names Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath, but the region drawn is the Bath-Bristol, Wiltshire and east-Somerset delta of Cliopatria's shapes, which the page does not name.

region.text: seven cells from Bristol to Gloucester

ledger.note: 587: the north of the Deorham gains slips away. Cliopatria's Wessex shape returns seven cells to its Hwicce row; neither the Wessex page nor the Deorham page mentions the Hwicce or any loss in the 580s (page silent).

region.text: three cells on the upper Thames, the Cotswold edge

ledger.note: 628: three cells of the upper Thames pass to Mercia in Cliopatria. The Wessex page and the Mercian Supremacy page say nothing about West Saxon-Mercian fighting in 628 (page silent); the infobox's 'client state of Mercia 645 to 648' is a later and separate fact.

region.text: eastern and central Somerset, east of the River Parrett

ledger.note: 658: Cenwalh takes eastern and central Somerset. 'in 658 his army met the Britons for a climactic battle at Peonnum' (the infobox says 'c. 660'); 'It was a decisive victory for the Saxons, who gained control of Somerset as far west as the River Parrett'; he 'advanced west through the Polden Hills to the River Parrett, annexing eastern and central Somerset', 'modest in size'. The page names the Britons of Somerset, not Dumnonia (the Dumnonia dossier makes the identification and holds the mirror loss); the site is uncertain. The Wessex page: Cenwealh 'was able to expand West Saxon territory in Somerset at the expense of the Britons'. Added by the eu-11-d fix pass (reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2); the 7 cells were in the shapes of 577-657 as drawn by Cliopatria.

region.text: western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel

ledger.note: By 685: Centwine takes western Somerset. The Peonnum page: the border 'remained at the Parrett until 681-685', when Centwine extended West Saxon control to the Bristol Channel; the Wessex page: Centwine 'fought and won battles against the Britons, but the details have not survived'. The page gives a span, not a year; 685 is its end and the year of Dumnonia's mirror loss. Added by the eu-11-d fix pass (reviewer finding /keyframe_review/2).

region.text: the South Saxons

ledger.note: 686: Cædwalla conquers the South Saxons. 'Ine kept the South Saxons, who had been conquered by Cædwalla in 686, in subjugation for a period'; Cædwalla 'returned to Sussex and won the territory again' and 'the province was reduced to a worse state of subjection' (Cædwalla page). Sussex keeps its own men: 'Sussex was still under West Saxon domination in 710, when Nothhelm is recorded as having campaigned with Ine'. Cliopatria draws Sussex inside Wessex from 692.

region.text: the Isle of Wight: 'He also conquered the Isle of Wight'

ledger.note: 686: Cædwalla conquers the Isle of Wight. The Wessex page: 'c. 685 to 688 (Cædwalla): Conquered Sussex, Kent and the Isle of Wight'; the Cædwalla page gives no year for Wight. 686 is the year the Ine page gives for the Sussex conquest, and Cliopatria's Wessex shape holds Wight from 692.

region.text: Kent: 'in 686 he installed his brother Mul as king of Kent'

ledger.note: 686: Cædwalla installs his brother Mul as king of Kent. 'in 686 he installed his brother Mul as king of Kent'. Mul was 'burned' in a revolt a year later (the Ine page: 'killed during a Kentish rebellion in 687') and Cædwalla 'returned, possibly ruling Kent directly'.

region.text: Kent, where 'Oswine took the Kentish throne, apparently a Mercian client'

ledger.note: 688: Kent is lost. 'In 688 Oswine took the Kentish throne, apparently a Mercian client'; 'Ine ... did not recover Kent'. The Wessex page: 'Kent regained independence almost immediately'; Ine made peace with Kent in 694 when its king Wihtred 'gave Ine a substantial sum'. Cliopatria nonetheless keeps Kent inside Wessex until 704.

region.text: what is now Devon (31 cells as drawn, 30 of them Dumnonia's; the 6 western-Somerset cells of the Wessex 710 shape are held since 685)

ledger.note: 710: Ine fights Geraint of Dumnonia and advances into Devon. 'In 710, Ine and Nothhelm fought against Geraint of Dumnonia, according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle'; 'It has traditionally been thought that Ine's advance brought him control of what is now Devon'. The page describes no formal annexation; the Wessex page: Wessex 'gradually overwhelmed Dumnonia' and Britons kept 'some independence' in Devon to the 10th century. Fix (eu-11-d): the region no longer includes the 6 western-Somerset cells gained in 685.

region.text: Sussex, independent again before the invasions of 722 and 725

ledger.note: c. 715: Sussex is independent again. The Kingdom of Sussex infobox: 'Subject to Wessex: c. 686 - c. 715' ('Client state of Wessex (686-715)'); its text: 'Sussex evidently broke away from West Saxon domination some time before 722'. The Ine page has Sussex 'still under West Saxon domination in 710' and Ine invading Sussex in 722 and again three years later. Year moved from Cliopatria's 718 by the reviewer of eu-11-d to match the kingdom-of-sussex dossier (vassal_end 715).

region.text: three cells of the Thames above London

ledger.note: 806: three cells of the Thames west of London pass to Mercia in Cliopatria. The Mercian Supremacy page names no Wessex-Mercian event between Offa (757-796) and Ellandun (825); unverified.

region.text: Cornwall: Egbert 'reduced Cornwall to vassal status'

ledger.note: 825: Egbert reduces Cornwall to a vassal. The Wessex page: '813 and 825: Campaigns against the West Welsh. Egbert conquered the western Britons in Devon and reduced Cornwall to vassal status.' The Egbert page has him campaigning in Dumnonia in an 825 charter, a battle at Gafulford in 823 and a victory over 'the West Welsh' at Hingston Down in 838, 'when Dumnonian independence may be considered to have ended'. Cliopatria's Cornwall row runs to 935 as an independent state.

region.text: Sussex and Surrey: 'seiz[ed] control of Surrey, Sussex, Kent and Essex from the Mercians'

ledger.note: 825: Egbert beats Beornwulf of Mercia at Ellendun and takes Surrey and Sussex. The Wessex page dates the battle '825 or 826'; the Egbert page: 'when Ecgberht defeated Beornwulf of Mercia at Ellandun', 'Æthelwulf was sent to Kent' and the men of 'Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex then all submitted', administered as a subkingdom under Æthelwulf. Sussex had been Mercian since the 770s (Cliopatria), which the pages opened do not date.

region.text: Kent, whose men 'submitted' to Æthelwulf

ledger.note: 825: Kent submits to Wessex. 'the men of Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex then all submitted' to Æthelwulf, but 'a Kentish charter dated March 826 still refers to Beornwulf's reign, so Baldred may have remained in power': the speed is disputed.

region.text: Essex

ledger.note: 825: Essex submits to Wessex. The Egbert page lists Essex among the submitting kingdoms but adds that its king Sigered was 'expelled on an unknown date, possibly 829' and that Essex's later status is 'uncertain'; Cliopatria gives Essex to Mercia from 840.

region.text: Mercia: 'King Egbert conquered the kingdom of Mercia, and all that was south of the Humber'

ledger.note: 829: Egbert conquers Mercia. 'Ecgberht drove Wiglaf ... into exile, temporarily ruling Mercia and gaining control of the London Mint'; the Chronicle: 'King Egbert conquered the kingdom of Mercia, and all that was south of the Humber'. Cliopatria dates the shape to 830.

region.text: Northumbria, which 'acknowledged his overlordship'

ledger.note: 829: the Northumbrians submit at Dore. The Chronicle says Ecgberht 'received the submission of the Northumbrians at Dore'; Roger of Wendover has an earlier invasion, and one historian argues the meeting 'reflected mutual recognition of sovereignty'. The Wessex page makes him Bretwalda.

region.text: Mercia, which Wiglaf 'obtained ... again'

ledger.note: 830: Wiglaf restores Mercia. The Chronicle says Wiglaf 'obtained the kingdom of Mercia again'; the page suggests 'a Mercian rebellion against West Saxon rule'. The south-east stays Wessex: 'the expansion across south-eastern England proved permanent'. Cliopatria keeps Mercia inside Wessex to 839.

region.text: Northumbria

ledger.note: 830: the Northumbrian overlordship lapses with Wiglaf's return. The page does not say when the relationship ended (page silent); one historian reads Dore as mutual recognition, so it is bridged to the year Mercia was restored.

region.text: Essex, the 16 cells Cliopatria draws as West Saxon until 839

ledger.note: 840: Essex leaves West Saxon control for Mercia, on Cliopatria's year only. The Egbert page hedges both ways: 'Wessex retained control of the south-eastern kingdoms, with the possible exception of Essex' and 'Wiglaf may also have brought Essex back into the Mercian orbit during the years after he recovered the throne' (no year; 'the Mercian orbit' may mean a client, not a province). Cliopatria's Wessex shape loses the 16 Essex cells in 840 and its Mercia 840 shape holds them. The reviewer proposed an 830 loss at confidence 2; not taken because no page dates it to 830. Added by the eu-11-d fix pass (reviewer finding /keyframe_review/19).

region.text: Wareham and Exeter, the ground the Danes held in Wessex

ledger.note: 876: the Danes seize Wareham. 'The Danes under Guthrum, Oscetel and Anwend seized Wareham in 876, broke their oath, and moved to Exeter' (Alfred page); the Wessex page adds that they returned to Wessex in 876 and withdrew in 877, and Alfred paid them to leave in 871.

region.text: Wareham, Exeter and the Somerset front

ledger.note: 878: Alfred wins at Edington. The Chippenham attack came in January 878 and Alfred took refuge in the Somerset Levels (Wessex page); the victory at Edington 'in 878' is followed by Guthrum's baptism at Aller 'three weeks' later, and the Danes 'withdrew to East Anglia'. The Alfred-Guthrum treaty follows 'perhaps in 879 or 880'.

region.text: Brycheiniog, whose king Elisse 'became a vassal of Alfred'

ledger.note: 880s: Brycheiniog becomes a vassal of Alfred. The Brycheiniog page: 'so in the 880s Elisse became a vassal of Alfred, to help protect his realm'; later 'Tewdwr ap Elisse ... witnessed a charter at the English royal court in 934' and Dryffin 'was forced by King Athelstan to pay tribute'. The page gives the decade only, so 880 is a bridging year (confidence 1); the Alfred page says only that the 'southern Welsh princes' submitted early in the reign.

region.text: English Mercia, 'Ceolwulf's kingdom consisting of western Mercia' (the 92 cells Cliopatria adds to Wessex in 884)

ledger.note: 880: Alfred takes over western Mercia when Ceolwulf II is deposed. The Alfred page: 'Alfred succeeded to Ceolwulf's kingdom consisting of western Mercia', in the passage that dates the Alfred-Guthrum treaty 'perhaps in 879 or 880, when King Ceolwulf II of Mercia was deposed' (the page calls 880 the date 'most commonly held'). Confidence 2: the year is the page's hedged 879-880; that Mercia is a vassal and not annexed is my reading (the Wessex page's 'direct control of Mercia in 918' implies indirect control before; the Alfred page has Alfred entrust London in 886 'to the care of his son-in-law Æthelred, ealdorman of Mercia' and never says Æthelred submitted). Cliopatria draws the land as Wessex only from 884. Fix (eu-11-d reviewer finding /ledger/22/note): the earlier note said the page was silent on the relationship and dated it to Cliopatria's 884.

region.text: the city of London: 'in 886, Alfred reoccupied the city of London'

ledger.note: 886: Alfred retakes London from the Danes. 'In 886, Alfred reoccupied the city of London', and he styles himself 'King of the Anglo-Saxons' from 886; the page adds that he gave London to Æthelred of Mercia.

region.text: the Kent coast where the Vikings landed

ledger.note: 892: a new Viking army lands in Kent. The page dates the attack to 'the autumn of 892 or 893' and gives Farnham, Buttington and 'the 894-895 blockade'; the six Kent-coast cells are Cliopatria's reading of the landing.

region.text: the Kent coast

ledger.note: 896: the Viking army disperses. The page gives the Vikings' departure 'in 896 (or 897)'.

region.text: 'the Mercian lands around London and Oxford'

ledger.note: 911: Æthelred of Mercia dies and Edward takes London and Oxford. 'Æthelred's death 911: Edward took control of the Mercian lands around London and Oxford'; Æthelflaed becomes Lady of the Mercians (911-918) and rules the rest of Mercia.

region.text: Bedford

ledger.note: 915: Edward takes Bedford. 'Bedford (915): ... Edward occupied it the year after building works in 914.' The Wessex page dates his overthrow of the Danes of Mercia and East Anglia to 913-918.

region.text: the Danish Midlands and East Anglia south of the Humber

ledger.note: 915: Edward's reconquest of the Danelaw begins in earnest. The Wessex page: Edward 'overwhelmed the Danes of Mercia and East Anglia between 913 and 918'; the first dated capture on the Edward page is Bedford in 915 (burhs at Hertford 911 and Witham 912 are fortifications, not captures).

region.text: 'the Danish armies of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia submitted during 917'

ledger.note: 917: the Danish armies of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia submit. Colchester was taken in late summer 917 'but not held'; Derby fell to Æthelflaed, not to Edward.

region.text: English Mercia

ledger.note: 918: Æthelflaed dies on 12 June and Mercia passes to Edward. 'took direct control of Mercia in 918, after Æthelflaed died'; the Edward page: the West Saxon Chronicle reports a Mercian submission and the Mercian Register has Ælfwynn removed to Wessex in December 918. Leicester had submitted to Æthelflaed in early 918.

region.text: all of Mercia, ruled directly from 918

ledger.note: 918: Edward rules Mercia directly. 'Took direct control of Mercia in 918, after Æthelflaed died.'

region.text: the Danish Midlands and East Anglia south of the Humber

ledger.note: 918: the Danelaw south of the Humber is Edward's. The Wessex page ends the 913-918 reconquest in 918; the Edward page names Bedford, Northampton, Cambridge, East Anglia, Colchester, Derby and Leicester but not Lincoln or Nottingham (page silent). Cliopatria dates the new shape to 922.

region.text: the Danish lands south of the Humber

ledger.note: 918: the Danish Midlands and East Anglia pass to Wessex. The Wessex page: Edward 'overwhelmed the Danes of Mercia and East Anglia between 913 and 918'. The towns on the Edward page do not cover the Humber shore; the year is the page's, the region Cliopatria's.

region.text: Seisyllwg, the realm of Hywel Dda and Clydog

ledger.note: 918: Hywel and Clydog of Seisyllwg submit to Edward. The Hywel Dda page: 'Hywel and Clydog seem to have ruled Seisyllwg together following their father's death and jointly submitted to Edward the Elder of England in 918'; the Edward the Elder page: 'Three Welsh kings, Hywel Dda, Clydog and Idwal Foel, who had previously been subject to Æthelflæd, now gave their allegiance to Edward'. The relation runs to 927 and passes to the Kingdom of England with the dissolve; this ledger does not close it. Split from the earlier placeholder counterpart by the eu-11-d fix pass (reviewer finding /ledger/34).

region.text: Gwynedd, the realm of Idwal Foel

ledger.note: 918: Idwal Foel of Gwynedd gives allegiance to Edward. The Edward the Elder page: 'Three Welsh kings, Hywel Dda, Clydog and Idwal Foel, who had previously been subject to Æthelflæd, now gave their allegiance to Edward' (in its 918 section; the sentence gives no year and names no kingdoms). The Idwal Foel page makes him King of Gwynedd from c. 916 to c. 942 and does not mention a submission in 918, so the year and the kingdom are read from the two pages together (confidence 2). The relation runs to 927 and passes to the Kingdom of England with the dissolve; this ledger does not close it. Split from the earlier placeholder counterpart by the eu-11-d fix pass (reviewer finding /ledger/34).

region.text: Cantref Coch, the Forest of Dean east of the Wye

ledger.note: 926: the border with Gwent is fixed at the Wye. The Gwent page: 'According to William of Malmesbury, Æthelstan met with the Welsh kings at Hereford in 926', 'where the border between the Kingdom of Gwent and the Kingdom of England was agreed at the Wye', 'removing Cantref Coch from Gwent's historic boundaries' (Cantref Coch is 'today ... the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire'). Mirror of Gwent's 926 loss. Of the 3 cells of this region, 2 were already inside the Wessex shape of 911-925 and 1 enters it in Cliopatria's 926 shape; the page attributes the account to William of Malmesbury and does not name Wessex. Added by the eu-11-d fix pass (reviewer finding /ledger, no mirror for Gwent).

region.text: York and the Danelaw remnant

ledger.note: 927: Æthelstan takes York. 'Sihtric died in 927 ... Æthelstan then invaded and took York' (no month). Cliopatria keeps the Danelaw remnant, and Northumbria, outside Wessex until 935.

region.text: the whole kingdom

ledger.note: 927: Wessex becomes the Kingdom of the English. The infobox gives 'the unification of the Angles, Saxons and Danes' as 12 July 927 and names the Kingdom of England as successor; the Æthelstan page has him styled 'King of the English' from 927 and the Eamont meeting on 12 July 927, where Constantine II, Hywel Dda, Ealdred of Bamburgh and Owain of Strathclyde 'accepted his overlordship'. Eamont's submissions belong to the England dossier.

wars.name: Battle of Deorham
wars.outcome: West Saxon victory: three British kings killed and three cities taken, by the Chronicle's account (the only evidence).
wars.note: Date and importance doubted by Sims-Williams and Collins; the page says the towns' importance 'more likely reflects ninth and tenth-century polities'.

wars.name: Battle of Peonnum

zones.text: eastern and central Somerset to the River Parrett

wars.outcome: Cenwalh's West Saxons beat the Britons of Somerset and annex eastern and central Somerset as far as the Parrett, which stayed the border until 681-685.
wars.note: The page says the battle was 'fought about AD 660' (infobox c. 660) and gives 658 in the text; it names 'the Britons of what is now Somerset', not Dumnonia, and the site is uncertain. Same war as in the Dumnonia dossier.

wars.name: West Saxon advance to the Bristol Channel

zones.text: western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel

wars.outcome: Centwine's victories let the West Saxons occupy western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel.
wars.note: The Peonnum page gives only the span 681-685; the Wessex page says Centwine 'fought and won battles against the Britons, but the details have not survived'. Same war as in the Dumnonia dossier.

wars.name: Cædwalla's conquests of Sussex, Kent and the Isle of Wight
wars.outcome: Sussex reduced to subjection and Wight conquered; Kent held only 686-688 under Mul and then lost.
wars.note: The page gives no year for Sussex or Wight; the Ine page has Sussex conquered in 686. Cædwalla abdicated in 688 and died in Rome on 20 April 689.

wars.name: Ine's war with Geraint of Dumnonia
wars.outcome: West Saxon advance into Devon; the British win at Hehil in 722 (site unidentified) and the page describes no annexation.

wars.name: Ine's Sussex campaigns
wars.outcome: Ine invaded Sussex in 722 after the exile Ealdbert fled there and again three years later, killing Ealdberht; the page records no territorial result.

wars.name: Battle of Ellandun
wars.outcome: Egbert defeats Beornwulf; Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex submit and East Anglia breaks from Mercia.
wars.note: The Wessex page dates it 825 or 826; the Egbert page notes a Kentish charter of March 826 still naming Beornwulf.

wars.name: Egbert's conquest of Mercia
wars.outcome: Wiglaf driven into exile in 829 and Mercia held for a year; in 830 he 'obtained the kingdom of Mercia again'. The south-east stays Wessex.

wars.name: Battle of Hingston Down
wars.outcome: Egbert is beaten by the Danes at Carhampton in 836 and beats the Danes and the West Welsh at Hingston Down in 838, when 'Dumnonian independence may be considered to have ended'.

wars.name: Viking invasion of Wessex
wars.outcome: Alfred buys off the Great Summer Army in 871; Guthrum seizes Wareham in 876 and Exeter, attacks Chippenham in January 878; Alfred wins at Edington and Guthrum is baptised. The Alfred-Guthrum treaty, 'perhaps in 879 or 880', fixes the Thames-Lea-Ouse line.
wars.note: Reading, Ashdown, Basing and Merton (871) and the 851 victory at Aclea (Wessex page) moved no border.

wars.name: Alfred's war against the Viking army of 892-896
wars.outcome: The Viking army is held at Farnham and Buttington and blockaded in 894-895; it departs in 896 or 897.

wars.name: Æthelwold's revolt
belligerents: Æthelwold with the Danes of Northumbria and East Anglia
wars.outcome: Æthelwold seizes Wimborne and Christchurch, goes to Northumbria, returns to Essex in 901 and is killed at the Holme (13 December 902) where the Danes 'kept the place of slaughter'; no border moves.

wars.name: Edward the Elder's reconquest of the Danelaw

zones.text: the Danish Midlands and East Anglia south of the Humber

wars.outcome: Bedford (915); the Danish armies of Northampton, Cambridge and East Anglia (917); Derby (917) and Leicester (918) to Æthelflaed; Mercia passes to Edward on her death in 918.
wars.note: The Wessex page gives 'between 913 and 918'; the Edward page's first dated capture is Bedford in 915.

wars.name: Æthelstan's conquest of York
wars.outcome: After Sihtric's death Æthelstan invaded and took York; at Eamont on 12 July 927 four kings 'accepted his overlordship'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line survives for any frontier: the Thames and Avon boundary against Mercia (Wessex page, 8th century), the Devon-Cornwall frontier and the Welsh march are approximate; Cliopatria's cell shapes are outlines, not lines.

The Alfred-Guthrum treaty ('perhaps in 879 or 880') names a line, 'up the Thames to the Lea, ... to near Luton, ... to Bedford, ... the Ouse to Watling Street', which is sharp; the Welsh, Cornish and Mercian-vassal frontiers stay soft.

The treaty line is gone after Edward's reconquest; the Humber and the York frontier of 927 and the Welsh and Cornish frontiers are approximate (the Tamar boundary of the Æthelstan page rests on William of Malmesbury and is 'treated sceptically').

notes:
Page budget (9) spent on Wessex, Deorham, Cædwalla, Ine, Egbert, Alfred, Edward, Æthelstan and Mercian Supremacy. Verdicts marked unverified lean on cell comparisons of Cliopatria's own shapes (counted with the gazetteer library) rather than on a page.
Start: the Wessex infobox says 'Established: c. 519' and the page 'Cerdic became first king in 519'; Cliopatria starts in 534, which is the year the infobox ends Cerdic's reign. identity.start is 519 (as the Tang start is 618 against Cliopatria's 623) with a new keyframe 519-533 that reuses the 534 shape. The Anglo-Saxon England dossier ends in 533, so 519-533 overlaps it: if the rendering agents cannot take overlaps, set the Wessex start to 534 and the found event to 534.
End: the infobox ends Wessex on 12 July 927; the text says Wessex 'ceased to exist as a political unit in 1066'. Cliopatria runs Wessex to 935 and starts Kingdom of England in 936, so 928-935 belong to nobody unless the kingdom-of-england dossier starts in 927 and carries them (its first Cliopatria shape, 936, is Wessex 926 + the Danelaw remnant + Northumbria, 496 cells). The Eamont submissions of 12 July 927 (Constantine II, Hywel Dda, Ealdred of Bamburgh, Owain of Strathclyde) are for the England dossier.
Mercian overlordship over Wessex is not in this ledger: the schema puts a vassal event in the suzerain's ledger, so Mercia's dossier should carry vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart kingdom-of-wessex for 645-648 (infobox 'client state of Mercia 645 to 648') and, if its pages support it, the 8th-century overlordship. Cliopatria's Mercia row swallows Wessex in 741-754 and 788-805 (74,610 and 84,530-96,899 km2 against 48,306 km2 for Mercia alone); this dossier draws Wessex there as a new keyframe.
English Mercia 880-918 is drawn as a vassal (fix pass eu-11-d): the Alfred page has Alfred 'succeed to Ceolwulf's kingdom consisting of western Mercia' when Ceolwulf II was deposed 'perhaps in 879 or 880' (vassal_start 880, confidence 2); it also has London entrusted in 886 to 'his son-in-law Æthelred, ealdorman of Mercia', the Edward page has Edward taking 'the Mercian lands around London and Oxford' in 911 and imposing 'direct rule on Mercia' in December 918. That the relation is vassalage and not annexation is my reading; Cliopatria draws the land as Wessex only from 884. The Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians page was not opened.
